title: Moving from Claude Opus 4.5 to Opus 5.5: what to change before 22 January 2027
short: Moving from Claude Opus 4.5 to Opus 5.5
description: Anthropic retires claude-opus-4-5-20251101 on 22 January 2027 and names claude-opus-5-5 as the replacement. The model name changes, and so may your request: Claude 4.7 and later accept only default sampling parameters. How to find and fix the calls.

blocks.p: Anthropic retires `claude-opus-4-5-20251101` on 22 January 2027, and calls to it fail after that. Anthropic's replacement is `claude-opus-5-5`. Changing the model ID is the first step. The second is a request change: Claude 4.7 and later accept only the default `temperature`, `top_p` and `top_k`, so code that sets them needs an edit.

blocks.h2: 1. Find every use of the old ID

blocks.p: The ID can be in code, config files, environment files and infrastructure templates. A scan lists each one with its file and line:
It needs no install and no key. Exit code 1 means a retired model is used in code. Until the date passes, the report shows the model as retiring, with the date and the replacement.
Where the model name is the only change, Driftline can make it for you. Preview first:
For this move, expect most calls to be listed rather than changed: the replacement is not a plain rename when your code sets sampling parameters, and `fix` leaves those lines alone and says why.

Anthropic's migration notes say Claude 4.7 and later accept only the default `temperature`, `top_p` and `top_k`. Search your code for the three names and remove them from requests that go to the new model. Anthropic's own guide has the full list of changes: [Anthropic migration guide](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/migration-2026-10-21).

ul: Check shared helper functions and wrapper libraries, since one default `temperature` there can reach every call.
If a setting was how you made answers more predictable, expect to rely on the prompt instead, and test the result.
Keep the old and new IDs apart in config until you have tested, so you can switch back before the retirement date.

blocks.p: A working call is not the same as the same answer. Run the prompts your app really sends on both models and compare. Driftline Pro does this in CI: each prompt in `.driftline/prompts.yml` runs on the current and the replacement model, two API calls per prompt on your own key, and the result says whether the answer stayed close, changed or broke.

blocks.code:
prompts:
  - id: ticket-summary
    model: claude-opus-4-5-20251101
    compare_to: claude-opus-5-5
    prompt: "Summarize this support ticket in one sentence: the printer is jammed again."
    must_include: [printer]

blocks.p: The `must_include` line is a check on meaning: the new answer has to contain that phrase, or the prompt is marked broken. See the [Opus 4.5 model page](/models/claude-opus-4-5-20251101/) for the date and source, where you can also sign up for an alert by email, Slack or webhook.
